extracted.intended_audience: Investigators applying to NIGMS MIRA (R35) grants (established, new, and early-stage PIs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/administrative criteria for applying to the NIGMS Maximizing Investigators' Research Award (MIRA, R35), including which investigator categories are eligible, applicable NOFO/PAR numbers, and program goals and term length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research must fall within the mission of NIGMS
rubrics_metrics.description: MIRA provides support for research in an investigator's laboratory that falls within the mission of NIGMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must propose research that is within the NIGMS mission area; eligibility and review will be tied to that mission alignment. See NIGMS program pages and FAQs for scope details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goal — increase efficiency, stability, and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of MIRA is to increase the efficiency of NIGMS funding by providing investigators with greater stability and flexibility, thereby enhancing scientific productivity and the chances for important breakthroughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose research and an overall program that would benefit from multi-year, flexible support rather than a narrowly scoped, project-specific R01. The program also seeks to distribute funding more widely among talented investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant duration — typical award term
rubrics_metrics.description: MIRA grants will generally be for 5 years for established investigators, new investigators, and early-stage investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan proposed research and budgets on a 5-year timeframe unless guidance in a specific NOFO/PAR indicates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — established investigators (EIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Established investigators who currently hold an NIGMS R01-equivalent grant or who wish to renew a MIRA are included in the expanded program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With PAR-26-121 publication the program now includes established investigators meeting these conditions. Contact NIGMS EI/NI MIRA program staff for clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — new investigators (NIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: New investigators who are not serving as a subproject leader on any multicomponent awards and who propose research within the NIGMS mission are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New investigators must not be subproject leaders on multicomponent awards; they should use the NOFO specified (e.g., PAR-26-121) and consult the FAQs and applicant slides for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and pathway for early-stage investigators (ESIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Early-stage investigators should apply through the ESI-specific MIRA NOFO (PAR-23-145); PAR-26-032 is a forecast announcement for ESIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESI applicants should follow the PAR-23-145 instructions (applications accepted through Feb 3, 2026 under that notice as indicated) and consult the ESI-specific FAQs, applicant slides, and eligibility guidance (NIH definitions of ESI and related policies). Contact NIGMS-ESIMIRA@nigms.nih.gov for ESI-specific questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the specified NOFOs/PARs and applicant resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must follow the appropriate Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO)/Program Announcement with Review (PAR) for the applicant category (e.g., PAR-26-121 for EIs/NIs, PAR-23-145 and PAR-26-032 for ESIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the listed resources (FAQs, Eligibility Decision Tree, applicant slides, feedback loop posts) and contact program staff (emails provided) for eligibility questions and application preparation. Ensure you apply under the correct PAR/NOFO window (dates and acceptance periods vary).
